children: a five-year contract by the Canadian government to provide uncrewed aircraft systems and training to the Canadian armed forces, with the option to purchase a significant number of additional systems.
Shares are ~6% higher ahead of Friday’s open, positioning Draganfly
to trade in the green for the first time this week.

Draganfly (DRPO) will provide Canada’s armed forces with 100 low-cost tactical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS) along with associated ground control stations, payloads, data links, support equipment, documentation, spare parts, and training.

Under the terms of the contract, the Canadian government has the option to order another 4,900 UAS systems for a contractual value of CAD24.25M ($17.5M). This would bring the total number of UAS systems from Draganfly (DRPO) to 5,000.
